span.p:
selectCapabilities()
{ documents, matrix, humanScore }
memoised · recomputed only when the
underlying slices change identity

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
syncRegistration(toolsFor(caps))
diffs desired against registered
· adds what is missing
· removes what no longer qualifies
· idempotent, so StrictMode is harmless

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Why capabilities, not phases.
A linear 0→3 sequence cannot express
'matrix but no documents' or the reverse.
Every branch required documents, so a fully
populated matrix sat at phase 0 with one tool.
Each tool now declares what it actually needs.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Reversible by construction.
Delete every document and `documents`
goes false. The registry diffs against the
smaller set and unregisters the three
document tools. No ghost tools survive.
